text:
maria: Quick sync — I ran a token-ceilings sweep across A10/A100/H100 to try to find the sweet spot for max_tokens_per_batch. Observed a regression on A100 once we exceed ~110k tokens: throughput drops ~18% and the kernel selector falls back to a slower matmul path for a subset of shapes. Dumped profiler output to /tmp/a100-sweep-3123.json.

kevin: Can you paste the exact profiler command you used and the minimal numbers (qps, p99) so I can reproduce?

maria: Ran: ```./run_profiler --gpu A100 --model redwood-7b --max-tokens 120000 --batch-formation continuous --out /tmp/a100-sweep-3123.json``` Results: qps 420 -> 345 (-18%), p99 42ms -> 68ms when crossing threshold. Kernel hint in the trace: `kernel_selector: chose matmul_slow for dense_fuse` and a bunch of small KV memcpy spikes.

sam: Sounds like KV-cache fragmentation + kernel fit problem. When batch tokens get large the per-request seq shapes vary more and kernels that were optimal for the common shapes stop matching and we get fallback. Two quick mitigations: 1) cap A100 slightly lower, 2) enable sequence-length bucketing so the scheduler forms more shape-homogeneous batches.

julia: Telemetry lines up with that. We see increased `kv_frag_count` and an uptick in `memcopy_ms` at the same time window. Also the kernel selector has a threshold param `flt_threshold` that currently biases towards the larger matmul kernel; for A100 we may be right on the cusp. If we tweak `kernel_selector.flt_threshold` from 0.72 -> 0.80 we avoid the bad codepath for the common shapes.

riley: Proposal (short): set per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch ceilings and enable seq-bucketing as an experiment. My suggested ceilings based on memory headroom and observed kernel fit: T4: 20_000, L4: 30_000, A10: 60_000, A100: 100_000, H100: 180_000. Rationale: keep A100 below the observed 110k knee; H100 has more headroom and better kernel diversity so higher ceiling ok. Also add a new queue policy flag `bucket_by_seq_len = true` (bucket width 64 tokens) and `prefer_kv_contiguous = true`.

kevin: SGTM. I'll run A100 and H100 experiments with the kernel threshold bump + bucketing. Plan: A100 runs at 95k/100k/110k but kernel_threshold=0.8, bucket_width=64. H100 runs at 150k/180k/210k. I'll collect perf.json and flamegraphs.

maria: Perfect. Can you also include a run that toggles `prefer_kv_contiguous` on/off? I want to see the memcpy delta.

kevin: Yep — adding `--prefer-kv-contiguous true|false` to the run matrix. I'll post links to perf-dashboard when done.

julia: FYI I've opened a small PR that exposes `kernel_selector.flt_threshold` per-accelerator in the config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/742 (WIP). If it lands we can A/B the param without rebuilds.

maria: Action items: 1) kevin -> run experiment matrix (A100/H100 + prefer_kv_contiguous toggle) by EOD Thursday, 2) sam -> prototype a lightweight seq-bucketer in the scheduler (bucket_width=64) as feature flag, 3) julia -> land config PR and add telemetry for `kernel_choice` per shape. I'll file an issue summarizing.

riley: I'll draft the issue and include the suggested ceiling table + experiment matrix.

devops-bot: experiment exp-3421 started by kevin (A100 run) :rocket:

kevin: initial A100 run posted: http://perf-dashboard/exp-3421 — early numbers look promising with kernel_threshold=0.8 and bucketing enabled (qps +12% vs baseline at 100k).

maria: Nice. Once we have final numbers we'll update the device ceiling map and rollout a staged change (canary across a subset of dedicated pools).

sam: Also log note: if we tighten ceilings we should surface this in the Console as a per-pool config and include a fallback policy that reduces ceiling when KV-frag>threshold.

kevin: Will add telemetry check and fallback rule to the experiment.

maria: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
